tossups.text: Although Paul Allen was the recognized efforts of the publication of Lewis's and Clark's memoirs, it is believed that two volumes were written by this politician, who edited Port-Folio magazine while serving in his state's legislature and supported efforts to create its first public school system. A participant in an audit of the Louisiana Purchase, he also wrote Pennsylvania's rejection of the Hartford Convention. This man reached his highest post after the resignation of Langdon Cheves, and he was opposed in that role by Treasury Secretary Roger Taney. To combat a hostile President, he shrank the U.S. monetary supply, causing a recession in order to force Andrew Jackson to re-charter the entity he led. For 10 points, name this politician who played a part in the Panic of 1837 and who served as head of the Second National Bank.

He went through a period as a playwright and director where he disavowed the use of scripts, giving actors only what he called, "a mandate to work around a cluster of images." His hometown, Port Elizabeth, plays a prominent role in his plays Blood Knot, Hello and Goodbye and Boesman and Lena. For 10 points, name this South African author of Sizwe Banzi Is Dead, The Island, and Master Harold and the Boys.

The rhythm of one of this man's works is intended to sound like the Charleston; that work is his Concerto in F. In another one of his works, he features bongos and maracas, and that work contains parts of the song "Echale Salsita." That work is the Cuban Overture. This composer wrote an opera set in Catfish Row that features the song "Summertime," and he began his tone poem, An American in Paris with the sound of car horns honking. For 10 points, name this American composer of Porgy and Bess, who included a famous clarinet glissando at the beginning of his Rhapsody in Blue.

Holy Qurbana refers to a version of this ceremony practiced by the Syriac Church. Some groups such as Seventh-Day-Adventists partake in foot washing before this ceremony. Huldrych Zwingli debated Martin Luther over whether this ceremony is symbolic or involves real presence, and the 4th Lateran Council expounded the theory of "transubstantiation" in regard to it. For 10 points, name this ceremony in which bread and wine are said to become the body and blood of Christ, which often takes place during Mass.

One person of this name defeated an Ammonite Siege of Jabesh-Gilead before being crowned king at Gilgal. That leader of this name committed suicide during a battle at Mount Gilboa, during which all of his sons except for Eshbaal were killed, and was deemed unfit after he replaced Samuel in performing a sacrifice and was ultimately succeeded by David. A Pharisee with this name persecuted Christians for the Roman Empire until he received a vision on the road to Damascus. For 10 points, give this name shared by the first King of Israel and an Apostle who changed his name to Paul.

In one of this author's works, the central character refuses to flee justice, stating that as a citizen, he is bound by the laws of his city. In another work, the same character denies charges of corrupting the youth. In addition to writing Crito and Apology, this philosopher describes his theory of Forms by telling a story of shadows dancing on the wall in the "allegory of the cave," and his works are often written as a dialogue. for ten points, name the author of the "allegory of the cave," found in his magnum opus, The Republic, a student of Socrates.

In James Baldwin's Just Above my Head, Julia Miller enters this profession at the age of seven. In William Gass' Omensetter's Luck, a man of this profession named Jethro Furber opposes but ultimately saves the title character from a murder charge. In Wolfe's The Bonfire of the Vanities, a man of this profession named Reginald Bacon exploits the central incident. In another novel, a man of this profession echoes his rival Asa Hawkes by blinding himself after taking Enoch Emery as his apprentice. Hazel Motes holds this position in O'Connor's Wise Blood, while other people to hold this profession include Frank Shallard and Sharon Falconer, who interact with Elmer Gantry. For 10 points, name this pulpit-based profession.

Description acceptable. In perfect competition, these entities have no market power and take prices from the market. If their average revenues don't cover their average variable costs, these entities shut down. If there's profit in a market, more of these entities enter, increasing the market's supply. In a monopoly, there's only one of these entities in a market. For 10 points, name these organizations that produce and sell goods.
acceptableAnswers: accept any description of someone selling something

tossups.text: In one work by this man, he writes "O love, O rose soaked by mermaids and spume, dancing flame that climbs the invisible stairway"; that work is called "March Days Return with their Covered Light" which is included in his 100 Love Sonnets. He also wrote odes to everyday items like a chestnut on the ground and salt in his Elemental Odes. Another work by him includes fifteen sections, which include "America, I Do Not Invoke Your Name in Vain" and "The Heights of Macchu Picchu." For 10 points, name this Chilean Nobel prize winning poet, known for anthologies Canto General and Twenty Love Poems and a Song of Despair.

In solution, this molecule assumes a pyranose structure though it exists in equilibrium with its cyclical isomers. This molecule is converted to ascorbic acid or vitamin C in the Reichstein Process. A radioactive analogue of this molecule called FDG is used in PET scans. The amount of this molecule present in the bloodstream is increased by a hormone produced in the alpha cells of the islets of Langerhans and is decreased by insulin. Polymers of this molecule include chitin, amylose, and cellulose. For 10 points, name this molecule, which is the starting point of aerobic respiration with a chemical formula C6H12O6.

One member of this species was returned to his homeworld by Captain Archer after landing in Broken Bow, Oklahoma. On the space station K7, another member of this species attempted to assassinate Captain Kirk by planting a bomb inside of a tribble, which were earlier declared a mortal enemy of this species. The Khitomer Accords established a peace between this species and the Federation, and General Martok became this species' chancellor after he killed Gowron. This species venerates Kahless and utilizes Bat'leths. For 10 points, name this species in Star Trek with pronounced ridges on its forehead.

This character teasingly asks her brother-in-law if he is an Aries but becomes flustered when he asks her if she knows a man named "Shaw". The sound of a locomotive causes this character to cover her ears while recounting a trip to Moon Lake Casino where she cried "you disgust me" after discovering her husband's homosexuality, which prompted him to shoot himself. This ex-wife of Allan Grey appears after losing her home Belle Reve and becomes enamored with Mitch. This woman has a breakdown after Stanley rapes her and declares "I have always depended on the kindness of strangers." For 10 points, name this sister of Stella Kowalski in A Streetcar Named Desire.

In human anatomy, this structure is essential for thyroid hormones t3 and t4. It plays a key role in the endocrine system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this thyroid-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The thyroid is a key component of the Endocrine system, involved in thyroid hormones t3 and t4.

tossups.text: This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for larynx and vocal cords. It plays a key role in the respiratory system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this pharynx-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The pharynx is a key component of the Respiratory system, involved in larynx and vocal cords.

tossups.text: This man co-owned a Major League Baseball team before becoming governor of Texas. "I can hear you! The rest of the world hears you!" this man responded into a bullhorn as he stood atop a demolished fire pumper in New York City following the 9/11 ["nine-eleven"] attacks. This man won the 2000 presidential election over Al Gore after a number of recounts of "hanging chads" in Florida. For ten points, name this 43rd U.S. president whose father was the 41st president.

During this man's rule, Wolfgang Lotz was convicted as a spy and imprisoned in his so-called "concentration camp" at Tura. His pact with Shukri al-Quwatli realized the regional ambitions this man alluded to in his Philosophy of the Revolution. This man rose to power by continuing an impassioned speech despite being shot at by an assassin. This man imprisoned Sayyid Qutb and other members of the Muslim Brotherhood, and incorporated Syria into his United Arab Republic. This successor of Muhammad Naguib and leader of the Free Officers lost the Six Day War and was succeeded by Anwar Sadat. A lake formed by the Aswan High Dam is named for, for 10 points, what Egyptian leader who nationalized the Suez Canal?

One ethnic minority in this non-Oman country practices Ibadi Islam and speaks a branch of the Zenati language group known as Mozabite. In 1988, the October Riots in this country led to the fall of its one-party system. This nation contains a region that borders the mountains of the Grande Kabylie [pr. "kuh bah lee"] and contains an eastern terminus in its Soumman River known as the Tell. Along with Tunisia and Morocco, the Atlas Mountains lie in this country. The largest country in Africa is, for 10 points, this nation with capital at Algiers.

One of this man's works sees the Dead Man and the Dead Woman invited by Aroni to appear at the Gathering of the Tribes. That work, A Dance of the Forests, came after another work that features the hypocritical religious figure Kadiye, The Swamp Dwellers. In another of this man's works, the titular character's son, Olunde, commits the ritual suicide to restore the honor of the family and the cosmic order. Baroka, Lakunle, and Sidi form a love triangle in another work by - for 10 points - what author of Death and the King's Horseman and The Lion and the Jewel, a Nigerian playwright?

This ruler stated "I glory in the name of Britain" in one speech, and the Papists Act of 1778 led to the Gordon riots during his reign. Prime Minister Spencer Perceval was assassinated during his rule, which included the passage of the Royal Marriages Act. George Grenville and Lord North were employed by this king, who allegedly mistook a tree for the King of Prussia and received the Olive Branch Petition from the Second Continental Congress. For 10 points, name this king of Britain during the American Revolution.

The American consul Joseph Ray lent support to one revolt in this colony; that revolt used a flag depicting a rainbow and three stars above a red cross on a white background. Ganga Zumba and Zumbi served as kings of one maroon settlement in this colony. One revolt in this colony was led by a dentist whose name translates as "the tooth puller." The oldest synagogue in the Americas was built in this colony during a brief period of foreign rule. Black and indigenous militia leaders took a leading role in expelling a Dutch takeover of this colony in the mid-17th century. The Fico speech declared the independence of this colony. This colony's frontier was advanced by settlers called bandeirantes, and the Minheiro Conspiracy attempted to gain independence for this colony. For 10 points, name this colony centered on the city of Rio de Janeiro.

parts.text: Identify this country which forcibly relocated its Japanese population to remote internment camps in its interior, similar to its southern neighbor. It was led during World War II by William Lyon Mackenzie King.

Canadian forces joined with British forces in defending this British colony, which fell to Japanese forces on Christmas 1941. In 1898, the British expanded this colony by leasing the New Territories for 99 years.
Canadians formed the majority of the force which attacked this French port city in 1942. While the attack failed miserably, it gave the Allies valuable experience for the later Normandy landings.

bonuses.leadin: This country ran internment camps such as New Denver and Tashme. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this angel who rebelled against God and declared that it was "Better to reign in Hell, than serve in Heav'n."
Satan appears in this epic by John Milton, in which he tempts Eve into eating the apple through a serpent in revenge for his banishment from Heaven.

At the end of Book I of Paradise Lost, Mammon recommends building this capital of Hell, whose name means "all of demons." After it is built by Mulciber, all of the spirits must shrink in size to enter it.

bonuses.leadin: At the beginning of the work in which this character appears, he wakes up next to Beelzebub after being "Hurled headlong flaming from th' ethereal sky." For 10 points each:

parts.text: This French pioneer of pointillism used small dabs of color to create the enormous Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte.
This pop artist used silk screen techniques to create portraits of Marilyn Monroe, Mao Zedong, and Campbell's Soup Cans.
Unusually, this work by Leonardo da Vinci was painted on a dry wall, leading to its extreme degradation. In this painting, Christ extends his hands over a table as his disciples look on.

bonuses.leadin: Artists often employ unusual methods to create art. For 10 points each,

parts.text: This native of Citium founded the philosophy of Stoicism, which he began teaching in Athens at the turn of the third century B.C.
This second century A.D. Roman Emperor was well known for his Stoic beliefs, which he espoused in his philosophic work Meditations.
This so-called "Second Founder of Stoicism" developed his own system of propositional logic. One account of this man's death states that he died of laughter after feeding wine to a donkey.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, name these ancient Stoic philosophers.

parts.text: Name this Greek philosopher who studied with Plato.
Aristotle uses this word to refer to his concept of a "final" cause.
Aristotle's major theoretical discussion of the four causes appears in this text. This book gives its name to a field usually divided into epistemology and ontology.

bonuses.leadin: This philosopher posited four "causes," two of which-matter and form-are the basis for his doctrine of "hylomorphism." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this ancient religion whose modern-day adherents are found in Iran and South Asia that is based on the teachings of its namesake prophet.
This is the central text of Zoroastrianism; it includes the Yasna, which contains the Gathas, which are believed to be composed by Zoroaster himself.

This other Persian religion, founded by Baha'u'llah in the 19th century, has its headquarters in Haifa, Israel. It emphasizes the underlying unity of world religions and sees a line of succession in the prophets.

bonuses.leadin: This religion worships Ahura Mazda and his eventual and inevitable victory over Angra Mainyu, or Ahriman. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this American poet of the collections With Ignorance, Tar, and the Pulitizer-winning Repair. This poet's characteristic style is narrative poems on moral quandaries written with long, enjambed lines.

Many of the poems in William's I Am The Bitter Name reflect on this event, also the focus of much of Denise Levertov's poetry. The speaker says "I said I wouldn't / dammit: No tears" in a Yusef Komunyakaa poem set at an object dedicated to this event.

Williams won the 2003 National Book Award for a collection titled for this action. In "The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock," the speaker says that "I have heard the mermaids [performing this action], each to each."

bonuses.leadin: This poet repeated the line "Why are you crying? Nothing is happening" throughout a poem about Leon Golub's torture paintings. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify these roommates who live in the 123 Building on Sesame Street. One is skinny, orderly, and yellow; the other portly, playful, and orange.
Ernie's most treasured possession is this bath toy which he's "awfully fond of." In the 80s Sesame Street did a calypso number called "Do De" this item.
Bert's pet, Bernice, is one of these birds. He dances a quirky dance called "Doin' the" this bird.

bonuses.leadin: Two answers required. In one sketch, one of this pair pretended not to hear the other because he had a banana in his ear. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this fourteen-line form of poetry.
This Elizabethan poet wrote about Gloriana as the Faerie Queene. He's also known for a namesake style of sonnet, which uses a stricter rhyme scheme than Shakespearean sonnets.
This 14th century Italian poet collected many of his namesake sonnets to Laura in Canzionere (can-zee-ohn-EHR-ay).

bonuses.leadin: In one of these poems, Shakespeare claims in iambic pentameter that "thou art more lovely" than a summer's day. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these compounds that have the same chemical formula, but differ in structural formula. Butane and methyl-propane form one example.
Enantiomers are certain stereoisomers that differ in the way they rotate the polarized form of this visible radiation studied in optics. The most basic unit of it is the photon.
Only one enantiomer of these is used by the body in protein synthesis. Including tryptophan and glycine, these building blocks of proteins are linked together by peptide bonds.

bonuses.leadin: They can be either constitutional or spatial. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this poetic form defined by unrhyming lines and regular meter. While this form can use any meter, the most common is iambic pentameter.
This English playwright helped popularize blank verse by using it in works like Tamburlaine the Great and Doctor Faustus.

Arden of Faversham, an early blank verse play, may have been written by Marlowe or Thomas Kyd, who is best known for this revenge play. This highly violent play is thought to have inspired some elements of Hamlet.

bonuses.leadin: Henry Howard is credited with introducing this poetic form to England with his translation of the Aeneid. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this former Attorney General that lives in Burden's Landing. He commits suicide after his bribe with an electric company is threatened to be revealed by Willie Stark.
Judge Irwin is antagonized by Jack Burden and the governor Willie Stark in this 1946 book set in Louisiana.
All the King's Men is a novel by this 20th century American author.

bonuses.leadin: This character is brought down from grace after he is revealed to have indirectly caused the death of Mortimer Littlepaugh. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with major arteries (aorta, carotid, femoral).
What is the main function of the aorta in the cardiovascular system?
Name another component of the cardiovascular system related to major arteries (aorta, carotid, femoral).

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human cardiovascular system.

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with pancreas digestive enzymes.
What is the main function of the liver in the digestive system?
Name another component of the digestive system related to pancreas digestive enzymes.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human digestive system.

parts.text: This government of Germany between the two World Wars was named for the city where the Bauhaus art movement began. It was noted for high inflation, Expressionist art, and the rise of the Nazi party.
Also known as Nazi Germany, this was the name given to Hitler's government that succeeded the Weimar Republic. The second part of this name means empire.
This city was the capital of West Germany before the reunification.

bonuses.leadin: Answer these questions about Germany during the 20th century, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this material used to build conical towers at Great Zimbabwe. The bird sculptures of Great Zimbabwe were carved from the soft "soap" type of this general material.
In the 1600s, the Rozvi developed this battle formation in which the main force was flanked by younger troops in a pincer movement. Impi soldiers used this formation at the Battle of Kambula.
acceptableAnswers: accept anything mentioning horns AND cows
such as horns of the buffalo

parts.text: The Rozvi's founder Changamire Dombo drove this empire and its puppet Mutapa away from gold mines. Padrão pillars were left by explorers from this empire, which Christianized the Kongo in the 1500s.

bonuses.leadin: The Rozvi Empire continued the Butua Kingdom's tradition of building cities from this material. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Many such routes would have one terminus at a tributary of this Russian river, the longest in Europe. It flows into the Caspian Sea and provides the current name for Stalingrad.

A portage from Ulan-Ude to the Shiika river, on this river system, connected Lake Baikal to the Pacific Ocean. The trading post of Nerchinsk, on the Shiika, was an early center for trade with Asia via this river system.

Short portages link the Lena and Yenisei with each other and the longest river system in Siberia, which is emptied by this river. This river's namesake "gulf" on the Arctic Ocean is the world's longest estuary.

bonuses.leadin: Russian trappers found portages between the major river systems of Siberia, allowing them to transport furs on water. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this novel, in which an Arab is shot on a beach in Algiers.
This French Existentialist author of The Fall and The Plague wrote The Stranger.
This protagonist of The Stranger asks Marie Cordona to a date. The novel begins with the death of his mother.

bonuses.leadin: The protagonist of this novel is neighbors with Raymond Sintes, who is rumored to be a pimp. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This leader recognized the Vatican as a sovereign country under the Lateran Treaty. Name this leader known as "Il Duce" who led Italy during World War II.

Years earlier, in 1922, Mussolini led this paramilitary group to march on Rome, ultimately leading to Victor Emmanuel appointing him to the position of prime minister. Name this militia group whose name was based on the color of its uniforms.
During World War II, Italy joined Nazi Germany and Japan to form this coalition that opposed the allies.

bonuses.leadin: The corpse of this man, along with that of his mistress, Clara Petacci, was hung upside down in Milan after being executed by firing squad. For ten points each:

parts.text: Identify this New York City anarchist group, whose name comes from a line in an Amiri Baraka poem. They cut down the fences at Woodstock, organized free concerts at Filmore East, and invaded the Pentagon in 1967 as an anti-war protest.
acceptableAnswers: obvious euphemistic equivalents from squeamish teams

parts.text: The more moderate New York hipster Abbie Hoffman wrote this work in 1970, which refers to America as the "Pig Izak Haber claimed that much of it was Empire" and is divided into the sections "Survive!", "Fight!", and "Liberate!"plagiarized.
This other member of the Chicago Eight was tried separately for the anti-Vietnam protests, but he remains best known for founding the Black Panthers together with Huey Newton.

bonuses.leadin: This group was formed by painter Ben Morea and poet Dan Georgakas, growing out of the Dada art group called the Black Mask. For 10 points each:
